prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

The profile below describes the moral priorities of the British electorate.

  loyalty: ambiguous (not scored)
  authority: ambiguous (not scored)
  sanctity: 0.20

</profile>

TEXT_A:
Summary of key proposals and commitments (ideology-neutral)

Health and care
- NHS: Extra £8bn in first year, rising to £28bn by 2030; at least £20bn capital over five years. Reduce waiting lists; rapid GP access; universal NHS dentistry with new contract and investment rising to £3bn/yr by 2030. Primary care: +£1.5bn/yr by 2030 and £2bn capital. Public health: +£1.5bn to restore 2015/16 levels. National Cancer Plan; mental health therapy within 28 days; school counsellor in every primary, secondary and sixth-form college. Assisted dying with safeguards. End new HIV transmissions by 2030.
- Social care: Free personal care; £20bn/yr investment; national pay/career structure; visa reforms to prevent exploitation; “Gloria’s Law” for essential care supporters. Disability: +5% to disability benefits; oppose PIP voucher plans; SEND transport rights. Children’s social care: +£3bn to councils; extended staying-put.

Housing and planning
- Build 150,000 new social homes a year; end Right to Buy; bring empty homes into use. Renters: local rent controls, end Section 21, long-term leases, energy improvement rights. Retrofit: £29bn for home insulation, £4bn for public buildings, £9bn low-carbon heating, £7bn heat-adaptation (first five years). New homes: Passivhaus-equivalent; solar and heat pumps; planning to require whole-life carbon assessment; protect green spaces/Green Belt.

Energy and climate
- No new oil/gas licences; end subsidies; carbon tax starting £120/t rising to £500/t within 10 years. Targets: wind ~70% of power by 2030; 80 GW offshore, 53 GW onshore, 100 GW solar by 2035. End de-facto onshore wind ban; expand grid, storage and interconnectors; support green hydrogen for industry. Community ownership minimum thresholds. Cease new nuclear; phase out existing over time; regulate biofuels; end imported biomass subsidies.

Economy, work and welfare
- Green investment average £40bn/yr (energy, retrofit, rail, public transport, active travel, industry, water/sewage, nationalisations). Public ownership: rail, water, Big 5 energy retailers. Regional mutual banks (£10bn capital) and £2bn/yr local grants to help SMEs decarbonise. R&D +£30bn over five years; circular economy and right-to-repair measures.
- Work: Repeal anti-union laws; Charter of Workers’ Rights; £15/h minimum wage with small-business offset; 10:1 pay ratio; day‑one rights; gig workers classed as workers; move towards four‑day week.
- Welfare: +£40/wk to UC/legacy benefits; end five‑week wait; scrap two‑child cap; +5% disability benefits; maintain pension uprating; +10% carers allowance; scrap bedroom tax; end sanctions; long‑term UBI.

Tax and public finances
- Wealth tax: 1% >£10m, 2% >£1bn. Align CGT and investment income with earnings tax/NICs; remove NI upper earnings limit; equalise pension tax relief to basic rate; reform inheritance tax. Property tax steps toward Land Value Tax; revalue council tax; adjust business rates reliefs. Windfall taxes (oil/gas, banks); VAT cuts for hospitality/arts; higher VAT on private education/financial services. Tackle avoidance; borrow to invest.

Nature, animals, food
- Rights of Nature Act; protect 30% land/sea by 2030; nationalise water; DEFRA +£1.5bn; Clean Air Act; Right to Roam; peatland rewetting; woodland +50%; urban biodiversity measures; fully protected MPAs. Commission on Animal Protection; ban blood sports; end factory farming practices (cages, routine antibiotics), lead ammo and snares; stricter companion animal rules.
- Food/farming: Nearly triple farm support for nature-friendly farming; link payments to reduced pesticides; expand horticulture and mixed farming; free school meals for all and breakfast clubs to Y6; food education; strengthen Groceries Code Adjudicator; boost domestic horticulture.

Education
- Schools: +£8bn incl. £2bn teacher pay; £2.5bn/yr for safe buildings (RAAC, maintenance); reduce high‑stakes testing; move academies to LA control; VAT on private school fees; SEND +£5bn; school nurses and counsellors. FE/skills: £12bn; sixth form +£3bn; restore EMA. HE: scrap tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; work towards addressing graduate debt.

Transport
- Operating subsidies up to £10bn/yr by 2030; £19bn capital over five years; nationalise rail; local bus control; £2.5bn/yr active travel; oppose new roads; restore fuel duty escalator; road pricing; end new ICE sales by 2027 and ICE road use by 2035; EV scrappage rising to £5bn/yr; default 20 mph in built-up areas. Aviation: frequent‑flyer levy; ban short‑haul flights where rail <3h; no airport expansion; apply carbon tax to kerosene.

Democracy, rights, migration, culture, digital
- Fair Politics Act: repeal voter ID; proportional representation; state funding rules; transparency on lobbying/think tanks; votes at 16; replace Lords with elected chamber; £5bn/yr more for English local government; defend HRA/ECHR; scrap restrictive protest laws; self‑ID for trans; X passports.
- Migration: end hostile environment and NRPF; safe routes; right to work for asylum seekers; simplify/at‑cost visas; free NHS for visa holders; remove income requirements; voting rights for visa‑holders; create Department of Migration.
- Arts/media/digital: £5bn over five years for local arts/sport; VAT‑free cultural tickets; media ownership cap (20%); implement Leveson; Digital Bill of Rights; precautionary AI regulation; creator IP protection.

Justice and policing
- End routine stop and search and facial recognition; restorative justice; presumption against custodial sentences <2 years; MoJ +£11bn over parliament; tackle court backlog; misogyny as hate crime; fund VAWG services; decriminalise sex work; youth services restored; decriminalise personal possession of drugs with diversion.

Foreign policy
- Support Ukraine; work towards EU re‑entry (Customs Union first, free movement, Erasmus). Israel/Palestine: immediate bilateral ceasefire; recognise Palestine; end UK arms exports to Israel; support war‑crimes investigations. Aid to 1% GNI by 2033; climate finance to 1.5% GNI incl. Loss & Damage; ecocide law; debt relief. Sign TPNW; cancel Trident; advocate NATO no‑first‑use and greater emphasis on diplomacy.

TEXT_C:
Summary of key policies in Labour Party Manifesto 2024 (ideology-free)

- Fiscal and tax
  - Adhere to fiscal rules: balance day-to-day budget; debt falling by year 5; OBR oversight of all major fiscal events.
  - No rises in NI, Income Tax rates (basic/higher/additional) or VAT.
  - Abolish non-dom status; close carried interest loophole; tackle offshore IHT avoidance; modernise HMRC to reduce avoidance.
  - One major fiscal event per year.

- Business, growth and investment
  - Industrial Strategy with a statutory Industrial Strategy Council; sector plans (auto, life sciences, creative, financial services).
  - National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn): ports (£1.8bn), gigafactories (£1.5bn), steel (£2.5bn), carbon capture (£1bn), green hydrogen (£0.5bn); target 3:1 private leverage.
  - Cap Corporation Tax at 25%; retain full expensing and AIA; publish business tax roadmap.
  - Replace business rates in England to level high street vs online and incentivise investment.
  - Ten-year infrastructure strategy; National Infrastructure & Service Transformation Authority; planning reform for nationally significant projects and labs/datacentres.
  - Communications: full gigabit and national 5G by 2030.
  - Innovation: 10-year R&D budgets; Regulatory Innovation Office; regulate frontier AI models; ban sexually explicit deepfakes; National Data Library.
  - Small business: action on late payments; reform British Business Bank; improve procurement access.

- Housing and local growth
  - Build 1.5m homes over the Parliament; restore mandatory targets; fund more planners (via higher non-UK buyer surcharge).
  - Brownfield-first; strategic use of “grey belt”; new towns; strengthen cross-boundary planning; reform CPO compensation.
  - Major increase in social/affordable housing; protect new social stock; first-time buyer priority; permanent mortgage guarantee.
  - Devolution: landmark legislation; Local Growth Plans; more powers over transport, skills, housing; multi-year council funding; end competitive bidding.

- Immigration and borders
  - New Border Security Command; EU security agreement; more caseworkers; end hotel use; returns/enforcement unit (+1,000 staff).
  - Reform points-based system; link shortage roles to domestic skills plans; sanction abusing employers.

- Work, skills and welfare
  - New Deal for Working People: ban exploitative zero-hours and fire-and-rehire; day-one rights (parental, sick pay, unfair dismissal); Single Enforcement Body; minimum wage remit to reflect cost of living; remove adult age bands.
  - Employment support overhaul; merge Jobcentre Plus and National Careers Service; youth guarantee (18–21); clear Access to Work backlog; reform/replace Work Capability Assessment.
  - Skills England; devolve adult skills; Technical Excellence Colleges; reform Apprenticeship Levy to a flexible Growth and Skills Levy.

- Energy, climate, environment
  - Clean power by 2030: double onshore wind, triple solar, quadruple offshore wind; CCUS, hydrogen, marine; maintain strategic gas reserve.
  - Nuclear: extend existing plants; deliver Hinkley/Sizewell C; support SMRs.
  - No new oil and gas exploration licences; honour existing; ban fracking and new coal.
  - Extend and tighten windfall tax; retain Energy Security Investment Mechanism.
  - Great British Energy (public company) capitalised £8.3bn; Local Power Plan.
  - Warm Homes Plan: +£6.6bn to upgrade 5m homes; PRS minimum efficiency by 2030.
  - Carbon Border Adjustment; mandatory 1.5°C-aligned transition plans for UK-regulated finance and FTSE100.
  - Water: tougher regulation, automatic fines, block bonuses, criminal sanctions; independent outlet monitoring.
  - Nature: new National River Walks (9), three National Forests; expand wetlands/peat/forests.
  - Farming: 50% public sector food local or higher-standard; land-use framework; reform ELMs; science-led TB strategy.

- Policing, justice and communities
  - Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee: thousands more officers/PCSOs/special constables; national efficiency programme.
  - Antisocial behaviour: Respect Orders; tougher shoplifting response; specific offence for assaults on shopworkers.
  - Knife crime: mandatory Youth Offending Team intervention; ban machetes/zombie knives/ninja swords; online sales controls with executive liability; Young Futures hubs nationwide; new offence of criminal exploitation of children.
  - Violence against women and girls: specialist rape units in every force; fast-track rape courts; domestic abuse experts in 999 control rooms; stronger stalking and spiking laws.
  - Police standards: mandatory vetting/misconduct rules; HMICFRS stronger powers; safeguards on child strip-searches.
  - Courts/prisons: use Associate Prosecutors; victims’ rights strengthened; sentencing review; build prison places; reduce reoffending via education, employment links; probation governance review; address historic injustices (Hillsborough Law, Infected Blood, Grenfell, Windrush, Orgreave inquiry).

- Education and childcare
  - 3,000 primary school-based nurseries; review parental leave; single child identifier.
  - 6,500 new teachers; reinstate support-staff negotiating body; teacher CPD entitlement.
  - Curriculum/assessment review; Ofsted single-grade replaced with report card; MATs inspected; SEND inclusion; free breakfast clubs in every primary; school mental health professionals.
  - Post-16: Skills England; devolved skills; Technical Excellence Colleges; Growth & Skills Levy; HE funding reform, access and teaching standards.
  - Arts/sport: study a creative or vocational subject to 16; protect PE time; National Music Education Network; ticket resale protections; independent football regulator.

- Health and social care
  - Cut waiting times: 40,000 extra weekly appointments (evenings/weekends); shared waiting lists; use independent sector capacity.
  - Workforce plan; reset relations with staff.
  - Fit for the Future fund: double CT/MRI scanners; deliver New Hospitals Programme; NHS innovation/adoption strategy; expand clinical trials via NHS App; upgrade NHS App for patient control and transparency.
  - Maternity safety and midwife expansion; regulate NHS managers; Royal College of Clinical Leadership; implement Cass Review.
  - Primary care: more GPs; face-to-face on request; modern booking; continuity incentives; pharmacist prescribing; direct referrals; trial Neighbourhood Health Centres.
  - Dentistry Rescue: 700k urgent appointments; contract reform; supervised toothbrushing (ages 3–5).
  - National Care Service: national standards; home-first; Fair Pay Agreement in adult social care; family visit rights; integrated discharge.
  - Mental health: 8,500 extra staff; Young Futures hubs; modernise Mental Health Act; suicide prevention focus.
  - Public health: smoke-free generation; hospital opt-out cessation; restrict youth-targeted vapes; junk food ad ban to children; energy drinks under-16 ban; online safety measures; gambling regulation reform.
  - Health inequalities: halve regional healthy life expectancy gap; women’s health priority; end new HIV cases by 2030.

- Governance and constitutional
  - Independent Ethics & Integrity Commission; empower Ministerial Interests Adviser; Commons Modernisation Committee; ban MPs’ paid advisory/consultancy roles.
  - Lords reform: remove hereditary peers; mandatory retirement at 80; participation requirements; stronger removal powers; appointment reform; consult on replacement second chamber.
  - Votes at 16; improve voter registration; fix voter ID inconsistencies; strengthen donation rules.
  - Devolution reset: strengthen Sewel; Council of the Nations and Regions; collaborative fiscal frameworks; devolve employment support in Wales; consider devolution in probation/youth justice; implement Windsor Framework; replace NI Legacy Act per Stormont House.

- Foreign, defence, trade and development
  - NATO and nuclear deterrent commitments; Strategic Defence Review; path to 2.5% GDP on defence; defence industrial strategy; military strategic HQ; national armaments director.
  - Armed Forces Covenant in law; Armed Forces Commissioner; scrap visa fees for non-UK veterans (4+ years) and dependants.
  - Support Ukraine (incl. frozen asset use, tribunal for aggression); AUKUS; audited China strategy; protect Overseas Territories.
  - UK-EU: improve trade (veterinary agreement, MRAs, touring artists), security pact; remain in ECHR; rebuild ties with France/Germany and JEF.
  - Trade strategy: targeted FTAs and sector deals; WTO/CPTPP engagement; OECD global minimum corporate tax; strategic partnerships (e.g., India, Gulf, Africa).
  - Clean Power Alliance internationally.
  - Development: rebuild FCDO capability; restore 0.7% GNI when fiscal conditions allow; focus on poverty, debt, women and girls, conflict prevention, climate finance; work with ICAI on value for money.

Judge whether A or B aligns more closely with this profile, taking into account that each foundation may be invoked in either direction.

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else. Do not wrap it in markdown code fences and do not add commentary before or after it. The object must have exactly these keys, in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "winner": "A" | "B"
}
